title: Why a Tibetan Protester Set Himself on Fire Outside the United Nations
author: Tsering Dolka Gurung
text:
Members of New York’s Tibetan community protest outside the United Nations three weeks after Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation, calling for renewed international attention to Tibet.
Credit: Tsering Dolka Gurung
Lobga Rangzen chose perhaps the world’s most recognizable symbol of international diplomacy as the place of his death. Dressed in traditional Tibetan clothing, he planted a Tibetan flag on the sidewalk across from the entrance to the the United Nations headquarters in New York on July 2. There, he set himself on fire, livestreaming his self-immolation on Facebook. His final act was intended to draw attention to Tibet’s decades-long struggle under Chinese rule.Rangzen, 52, was born in Tibet and fled to India in the 1990s, where he lived as a monk before immigrating to the United States in 2006. Over the next two decades, he became an active member of New York’s Tibetan community. His self-immolation was the first known by a Tibetan on U.S. soil.[...]
